lesson.menu_title: The Bilateral Meeting -- Leading a Meeting From Start to Finish
lesson.menu_desc: Lead a full bilateral meeting with the Parma consortium: open it, move between agenda items, and close with a summary and next steps, using data, 'if' and culture from Lessons 21-24 -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 25 -- The Bilateral Meeting
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Flávia Florêncio Ferreira | Lesson 25 -- The Bilateral Meeting
lesson.grammar_point: meeting structure language (opening, transitions and closing a meeting)

listenings.text: Hi, Flavia. It is Renata, from the international team. Here is a quick overview of tomorrow's meeting with Paolo. The meeting starts at ten, and it is one hour long. There are three agenda items: our figures, the partnership proposal, and the products. Paolo will chair the first part, and you will chair the rest. Please bring the new figures: we now have nearly five hundred certified producers. At the end, someone needs to take the minutes. I can do that for you. Good luck, and see you tomorrow.

Here is how to close a meeting well. Many meetings end with: okay, thank you, bye. That is a mistake. Use the last five minutes for the wrap-up. First, summarize. Say: to summarize what we discussed, and repeat the main decisions. Second, check the consensus. Ask: do we all agree? Third, give every action item a name and a date. Finally, say who will send the minutes. People remember the end of a meeting more than the middle. A strong wrap-up gives everyone a clear takeaway.

extra_audio.text: First, I thank the partner and I say: I would like to start by looking at the agenda. Then, I present our figures with approximation language. Next, I say: moving on to the proposal, and I set one condition with if. After that, I connect one Brazilian product to an Italian tradition. Finally, I summarize what we discussed and I say the next step.

items.situation: The meeting is almost over. Summarize the decisions.
Say the next step and close the meeting.
tips: The next step would be to share the minutes.
I look forward to following up on this.
